1. Core Clinical Tension: A 26-year-old man with alcohol use disorder presents with high fever, severe headache, epigastric/RUQ pain, vomiting, elevated amylase/lipase, and marked transaminitis. While acute alcoholic or biliary pancreatitis is the immediate surgical consideration, the presence of hemoconcentration, profound thrombocytopenia (23,000/μL), widespread petechiae, and polyserositis (ascites, pleural effusion) points toward an acute arboviral infection with pancreatic tropism.
2. Admission Breakpoint: The admission breakpoint occurs following emergency admission, physical exam (relative bradycardia, petechial rash, abdominal tenderness), triage labs (Hct 49%, platelets 23,000/μL, pancreatic and liver enzyme elevation), and abdominal ultrasonography, immediately prior to arboviral serological testing.
3. Differential Distinctions: Acute biliary pancreatitis was suspected from RUQ pain and transaminitis, but ultrasonography showed normal gallbladder wall thickness without stones and normal bile ducts. Alcoholic or hypertriglyceridemic pancreatitis was ruled out by only mild triglyceride elevation (267 mg/dL) and normal calcium, with petechiae and capillary leakage explained by viral infection.
case_prompt:
A 26-year-old man with a history of alcohol use disorder since age 20 and unspecified neonatal hepatomegaly presents to the emergency department with a 5-day history of throbbing headache, arthralgias, severe myalgias, and documented fever up to 40.4°C that responded only partially to ibuprofen and failed to respond to acetaminophen. On the second day of illness, his condition worsened with crampy epigastric pain radiating to the right upper quadrant, accompanied by persistent nausea and vomiting. He is a resident of a tropical endemic region.

On physical examination, blood pressure is 120/90 mmHg, heart rate is 56 beats per minute (sphygmothermic dissociation), respiratory rate is 20 breaths per minute, oxygen saturation is 97% on ambient air, and temperature is 36.6°C. Disseminated petechiae are visible over his face, trunk, and extremities. Cardiopulmonary examination is normal. Abdominal examination reveals scattered petechiae, abdominal distension with an abdominal perimeter of 95 cm, and marked tenderness to palpation in the epigastrium and right upper quadrant without guarding, rebound tenderness, or palpable hepatosplenomegaly. Peripheral pulses are normal without peripheral edema.

Admission laboratory testing demonstrates hemoconcentration with a hematocrit of 49%, profound thrombocytopenia with a platelet count of 23,000/μL (23.000), and C-reactive protein of 29.2 mg/L. Serum transaminases and pancreatic enzymes are markedly elevated: aspartate aminotransferase (GOT) 747 U/L, alanine aminotransferase (GPT) 509 U/L, amylase 229 U/L, lipase 258 U/L, gamma-glutamyl transferase 604 U/L, alkaline phosphatase 208 U/L, lactate dehydrogenase 995 U/L, and lactic acid 3.4 mmol/L. Triglycerides are 267 mg/dL, total cholesterol is 158 mg/dL, phosphate is 2.4 mg/dL, albumin is 3.7 g/dL, and fasting glucose is 112 mg/dL.

Abdominal ultrasonography reveals hepatomegaly with diffusely increased echogenicity and periportal cuffing, free fluid along the left hepatic border extending into Morison's pouch, and scant perisplenic fluid. The gallbladder has normal wall thickness without intraluminal calculi, and intra- and extrahepatic bile ducts are nondilated. The pancreas is slightly hypoechoic with preserved architecture. Small bilateral pleural effusions with basilar compressive consolidation and air bronchograms are also noted.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Severe epigastric pain radiating to the right upper quadrant accompanied by elevated lipase, amylase, and hepatic enzymes initially suggested biliary tract obstruction; however, ultrasonography revealed a normal gallbladder without stones and nondilated bile ducts.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: Gallbladder with walls of normal thickness, without endoluminal images, nondilated bile ducts, slightly hypoechoic pancreas, preserved shape and structure... Having ruled out the biliary cause of pancreatitis and searching for other causes

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Longstanding alcohol use disorder history raised suspicion for toxic-metabolic pancreatitis; however, serum triglycerides were only mildly elevated (267 mg/dl, well below the >1,000 mg/dl threshold for pancreatitis), serum calcium was normal, and widespread petechiae with severe thrombocytopenia pointed to an acute infectious arboviral etiology.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: Having ruled out the biliary cause of pancreatitis and searching for other causes, there were no calcium abnormalities, hypertriglyceridemia, endocrine abnormalities, or use of drugs associated with pancreatitis.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Clinical presentation in an endemic region characterized by high fever, severe thrombocytopenia (23,000/μL), hemoconcentration, and third-spacing (ascites, pleural effusion) leading to acute pancreatic inflammation, confirmed by positive IgM and IgG viral antibodies.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: Due to a history of fever and being a resident of an endemic area of the dengue virus, a viral panel was requested, resulting in positive IgM and IgG antibodies for dengue, with negative NS1 antigen (Table 2), qualifying it as dengue with warning signs.
